name: research-question
text:
Research question
How can multiple institutions train a useful shared model while limiting privacy exposure, encrypted communication cost, poisoning damage, and unilateral control?
textPreview: Research question | How can multiple institutions train a useful shared model while limiting privacy exposure, encrypted communication co...

name: problem-paragraph
text: Although federated learning keeps patient records within each institution, the gradients and model updates exchanged during training may still expose sensitive information through membership inference or reconstruction attacks. Applying CKKS encryption protects update values, but it increases the serialized communication payload and prevents many poisoning defenses from examining individual plaintext updates. Existing systems may also depend on centralized decryption, unverifiable aggregation, or limited audit evidence, which concentrates trust and reduces accountability. Current approaches therefore seldom provide record-level privacy, practical encrypted communication, poisoning resilience, and independently verifiable governance within one evaluated multi-institutional healthcare framework.
textPreview: Although federated learning keeps patient records within each institution, the gradients and model updates exchanged during training may ...

text: Federated learning keeps source records local, but exchanged updates can still leak information. CKKS improves confidentiality while increasing communication cost and hiding the update geometry used by many poisoning defenses. Centralized decryption, unverified aggregation, and limited audit evidence create additional trust concerns. The thesis therefore treats privacy, efficiency, adversarial resilience, and release governance as one engineering problem.

text: Published healthcare studies motivate multi-institutional learning. Sheller et al. reported that federated training across 10 institutions reached 99% of the model quality achieved with centralized data. The EXAM study trained on 16,148 cases from 20 clinical sites across four continents and reported an average local-test AUC increase from 0.795 for local models to 0.920 for the federated model. These results establish the value of collaboration, while this thesis addresses the remaining privacy, encrypted communication, poisoning, and governance challenges. Sources: Sheller et al., Scientific Reports 10, 12598 (2020), doi:10.1038/s41598-020-69250-1; Dayan et al., Nature Medicine 27, 1735–1743 (2021), doi:10.1038/s41591-021-01506-3.

text: DP-BREM and DP-BREM+ jointly address differential privacy and Byzantine robustness in cross-silo federated learning. Client momentum averages each client's updates over time, reducing honest-client variance and making accumulated malicious perturbations easier to detect. DP-BREM assumes a trusted server; DP-BREM+ removes that assumption with secure aggregation and client-generated distributed noise. text: PREAMBLE addresses private aggregation of high-dimensional vectors in a two-server architecture. It uses block-sparse distributed point functions, random sampling, and privacy amplification so that communication and computation depend more strongly on active blocks than on the full vector dimension. Its formal analysis is a strong example of co-designing representation and privacy transport. Relative to this thesis, PREAMBLE assumes two non-colluding servers, targets private vector aggregation rather than iterative CKKS healthcare training, and does not study poisoning or release governance. Source: https://proceedings.neurips.cc/paper_files/paper/2025/hash/1d3c1c0bade7b2b1974d3120ab6232b0-Abstract-Conference.html

text: This conceptual framework links the research problem to the proposed intervention and the evaluation plan. Distributed hospital data, non-IID partitions, privacy threats, poisoning risk, and encrypted communication cost define the research context. The hybrid intervention combines record-level differential privacy, CAABC-FL block compression, CKKS-protected updates, and governance controls. These mechanisms support protected local training, authenticated update exchange, verified homomorphic aggregation, and threshold-governed release. The study evaluates predictive utility, privacy exposure, poisoning resilience, communication cost, and runtime overhead under the stated threat and trust assumptions.

name: release-boundary-note
text: Only the validated aggregate can become the global model. The audit ledger stores evidence, not model ciphertexts.

text: This slide shows how the framework transports, aggregates, validates, and releases a model. Mutual TLS and signed round metadata authenticate every submission. The permissioned ledger stores hashes and status, while model ciphertexts remain off-chain. The coordinator performs reputation-weighted homomorphic aggregation and custodians decrypt only the aggregate. Validation either accepts the candidate model or triggers rollback and quarantine. Hospitals verify the signed model hash before starting the next round. Clinical inference follows the same authorization and controlled-decryption policy.

name: problem-formulation-round-summary
text: One training round constructs protected local updates, aggregates ciphertexts, and releases only a validated global model.
textPreview: One training round constructs protected local updates, aggregates ciphertexts, and releases only a validated global model.

text: The formulation has four parts. First, the global objective is the sample-weighted average of hospital losses, where n_k is the number of records at hospital k and N is the total across participating hospitals. Second, each gradient is clipped to norm C, Gaussian noise z_k^t provides record-level differential privacy, and the residual e_k^t preserves information lost by CAABC-FL compression Q_s_t. Third, the accepted client set A_t contributes encrypted updates to the CKKS sum c_t. Threshold custodians decrypt only this aggregate, and eta_t is the global learning rate. Finally, the design must reduce predictive loss and serialized communication while satisfying privacy, integrity, threshold-release, and audit requirements.

name: finding-bullets
text:
CAABC-FL passed the registered AUROC non-inferiority gate against dense DP-FedAvg-CKKS.
The AUPRC difference was negative, so the evidence does not support universal utility superiority.
The governance layer contained the tested longitudinal backdoor with 60% rollback and a 0.0293 clean-AUROC cost.
OpenFHE 3-of-3 CKKS achieved maximum error of 1.34 x 10^-13, while the main service remained centrally keyed.
textPreview: CAABC-FL passed the registered AUROC non-inferiority gate against dense DP-FedAvg-CKKS. | The AUPRC difference was negative, so the evide...

text: The strongest result is the encrypted communication saving. CAABC-FL reduced serialized upload by about 56 percent while maintaining AUROC within the registered non-inferiority margin. AUPRC and several operating-point metrics declined, so we present a bounded trade-off rather than universal superiority.

name: limitations-bullets
text:
One retrospective sepsis cohort, two source hospitals, one MLP, and no prospective or external clinical validation.
The main TenSEAL service uses central key custody. The OpenFHE threshold experiment remains an isolated 3-of-3 test without dropout tolerance.
Network timing comes from sequential single-host runs, not a wide-area multi-institution deployment.
No physical Intel TDX or AMD SEV-SNP experiment, medical-device assessment, or stakeholder usability study.
Membership, reconstruction, and poisoning findings remain specific to the registered attacks and five security seeds.
textPreview: One retrospective sepsis cohort, two source hospitals, one MLP, and no prospective or external clinical validation. | The main TenSEAL se...

name: limitations-close
text: These limitations restrict deployment claims but do not invalidate the measured protocol-level results.
textPreview: These limitations restrict deployment claims but do not invalidate the measured protocol-level results.

text: We separate research-system evidence from production claims. The results remain valid for the registered experiment, but they do not prove clinical effectiveness across hospitals or remove the need for networked key custodians, confidential hardware, and external evaluation.
